low.title: Promotion request left unresolved and inbox-visible when promoteStaged ends the staged change through end() or device revocation
low.boundary: promoteStaged end() helper (manager.server.ts:2612-2619) and the revocation path (2585-2593). Contract D2 says a staleness end resolves the request as deny. end() calls endStaged and fails the step, but never sets resolvedAt on the request or calls inbox.resolve. Only closeWaiting (2621-2627) does, and only when the same request is answered again. Revocation (2591) likewise fails the step and clears pendingRequestId without closing the promotion request. Closure is therefore deferred to a later respond rather than done at end time. Authority is not affected: a later respond on the stale request is refused, and closeWaiting resolves only the request being answered.
low.reproduction: Stage a device write, then revoke the device while the promotion request is open (or change the Agent consent). Step failed with pendingRequestId null, but the promotion request still has resolvedAt null and remains in the Host inbox. Answering it later returns 'this staged change is INVALIDATED_*' and only then closes it.
low.evidence: manager.server.ts:2612-2619 (end without request close), 2585-2593 (revocation without request close), 2621-2627 (closeWaiting, the only closer). Lens answer: closeWaiting is safe when the step is not waiting on the request; it resolves only the answered request and changes the step only when pendingRequestId matches.
low.repair: In end() and in the revocation branch, when the request is unresolved, resolve it as deny with inbox.resolve, the same as closeWaiting. Add a test that the inbox has no open promotion request after revocation.

verified.title: 8.3 directory alias bypasses the dot-folder, agent, execution and watched-source directory rules
verified.boundary: D1 classifyDeviceWrite (authorization.server.ts). Directory role regexes at lines 602, 605, 606 and 612 are tested only against `dirs`, the segments of the canonical relative path. Canonicalization keeps 8.3 short names, so a directory written as a short alias is never matched. The `~\d` refusal at line 573 covers only the leaf, not directory components. The round-2 repair (every dot-folder is CONFIGURATION) and the EXECUTION_DIR rule are both defeated. A remote-envelope device write to an alias is therefore PHONE_SAFE, passes remoteExecutionRefusal, and reaches the workstation promotion prompt labelled PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT. The workstation still has to approve it, so this is a classification and reviewer-label gap rather than a direct bypass.

verified.title: Lifecycle of an answer that was already used is stamped WITHDRAWN, not CONSUMED, after a verify-phase ask or a step failure
verified.boundary: Audit integrity of the one-time-answer lifecycle (F02 section 12). CONSUMED is stamped only at step completion (manager.server.ts:3590) and in endDeviceAnswers (2444). The execution answer stays on the step (approvedOnce is not cleared at admission) while the step runs its verification, and askPermission (~3789-3870) does not clear it either. A verify-phase ask or a later failure therefore runs setStep with approvedOnce replaced or null, and setStep stamps WITHDRAWN on the already-exercised answer: 'The step ... ended this one-time answer'. The WITHDRAWN record is permanent (first stamp wins), so the audit trail says a write that actually executed was withdrawn unused.
verified.reproduction: Code-path reproduction, not executed: a write step is answered allow_once and admitted (filesystem.write runs). Its verification check then needs an ask (verifyAndComplete -> askPermission phase verify, step waiting_for_approval with approvedOnce still set). The workstation answers allow on the verify request, which runs setStep(approvedOnce: {verify request}) at manager.server.ts ~4144-4147. The execution answer's request gets lifecycle WITHDRAWN (setStep at line 510-511) and never CONSUMED. The same WITHDRAWN stamp results when verification fails and stepFailed clears approvedOnce (~3703).
verified.evidence: manager.server.ts:510-511 (stamp on replace or clear), 3590 (only completion CONSUMED), 2441-2445 (endDeviceAnswers), 3703 (failure clears approvedOnce), 4144-4147 (verify replace). No CONSUMED stamp exists at admission in liveOnce (2480-2491) or in the bus path.
verified.repair: Stamp CONSUMED at the moment an answer authorizes an admitted run (the capabilityRequest/liveOnce admission point, or when the step leaves ready for running), so WITHDRAWN only ever records an answer that was never used. Keep first-stamp-wins. Add a test: answered write, executed, verification asks, then the verify answer replaces it; the execution request must read CONSUMED.

votes.reasoning:
Not refuted on code reading of the working tree (no probe run, no npm test, no repo edits).

1. The admission path never stamps CONSUMED. markRunning and capabilityRequest/liveOnce leave approvedOnce in place (manager.server.ts ~1550-1564, 2480-2491). The only CONSUMED stamps are at 3590 (verifyAndComplete completion, which stamps whatever approvedOnce is set at that moment) and 2444 (endDeviceAnswers, running/verifying branch).

2. The verify ask keeps the execution answer on the step. askPermission (~3815-3875) sets only state, pendingRequestId and pendingPhase, so approvedOnce still holds the execution answer. When the workstation answers the verify request, respond sets running with approvedOnce = verify request (manager.server.ts 4144-4147). setStep (510-511) then sees a different requestId and stamps WITHDRAWN on the execution answer, with message text "The step running ended this one-time answer (a later answer replaced it)." The execution answer was already exercised, since the write ran under it.

3. The failure path does the same. stepFailed (3703) clears approvedOnce to null after the write ran, so setStep stamps WITHDRAWN on the used answer. Retry and replan (4327) and the other clear sites also stamp WITHDRAWN.

4. The repo's own model contradicts this. The comment at manager.server.ts 2441-2443 says an answer already admitted (running or verifying) "did take effect: that is recorded as CONSUMED". F02-R2-4 (f02-staging.test.ts:775-786) asserts exactly that for the revocation path. The completion, verify and failure paths do not follow it, so the same class of used answer gets CONSUMED in one path and WITHDRAWN in another.

5. The existing F02-R2-3 test (f02-staging.test.ts:759-771) covers only a refused write that never executed, so it does not exercise the admitted-then-failed case, and WITHDRAWN is correct there. The gap is not covered.

Authority impact is nil: onceInvalidity (~2464-2470) returns the stamped state for any stamped request, and the answer is cleared, so no reuse is possible. The defect is audit label accuracy only, which fits MEDIUM audit integrity. Caveat: traced by code reading, not run.

Code-path verification against the working tree (read-only; no probe run, no npm test, no repo edits).

Confirmed as real:
1. manager.server.ts:510-511 (setStep) stamps WITHDRAWN on any one-time answer that a patch replaces or clears, and the stamp is first-wins (stampLifecycle, ~2446-2452).
2. CONSUMED is stamped only at manager.server.ts:3590 (verifyAndComplete completion) and in endDeviceAnswers at 2443-2444 for running/verifying steps. There is no CONSUMED stamp at admission (markRunning ~1255-1275 and capabilityRequest/liveOnce ~1547-1564 keep approvedOnce set without stamping).
3. Verify-phase path: verifyAndComplete sets state "verifying" at 3410 without clearing approvedOnce. askPermission (3789-3870) sets waiting_for_approval without touching approvedOnce. On the verify approval, respond at 4144-4147 writes approvedOnce to the verify request. Because the requestId differs, setStep at 510-511 stamps the execution answer WITHDRAWN with reason "The running ended this one-time answer (a later answer replaced it)." That answer had already authorized the executed write.
4. Failure path: stepFailed at 3700-3703 sets approvedOnce:null, so the same WITHDRAWN stamp is written on an answer that was already exercised.

Why not refuted: this is not documented intent. The round-1 repair (round1.json:154) asked that every answer that authorized an attempt get a CONSUMED or equivalent record before it is cleared. The current code instead gives WITHDRAWN, so that repair is incomplete on the setStep and failure paths. Audit integrity is an explicit MEDIUM criterion.

Caveats that limit severity: no authority impact. The WITHDRAWN answer is treated as invalid by onceInvalidity (2464), so nothing is re-authorized. The stamp reason text says "ended", not "unused", so the finding overstates the label as "withdrawn unused". Round 2 refuted a closely related admission-based label as LOW (round2.json:213), so LOW is a defensible grade if the reviewer does not accept the audit-integrity framing.

Adjacent lead, not verified as a finding: during the verifying window the execution answer stays live. The verify check is built from a fresh step at 3414 with approvedOnce still set, so capabilityRequest (1555-1564) would extend roots and set oneTimeAction for a check whose action equals the answered action. That needs a verification check with the same action as the execution, which is uncommon.

low.title: Staged-change queries scan the whole table on every call and the table is never pruned
low.boundary: Performance of the staging table: store.server.ts mutationSequence() (151-158) runs a json_extract over every device_staging row on each call, and device_staging has no index on state. low.reproduction: Each desktop approval or grant binding calls mutationSequence(), which runs SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE state IN (...) OR json_extract(record,'$.promotionStarted')=1 across all rows. The OR with json_extract cannot use an index, so cost grows linearly with the lifetime number of staged changes. Each mission view also parses every staged record of that mission.

verified.title: Retry strands a waiting promotion step and withdraws the staged change before validating Retry
verified.boundary: Mission state/step lifecycle: manager.server.ts withdrawStaged (2597) and endStaged (2570-2586) close the promotion request but never move its step; retry() (4291) calls withdrawStaged at 4298 before its own validation (no-failed-step throw at 4309, envelope check before it).
verified.reproduction: 1) A paired device with a remote envelope stages a write; askPromotion (~3319) leaves the step in waiting_for_approval with pendingRequestId = the promotion request and the mission drops to waiting_for_user (tick, ~line 999-1006). 2) The workstation clicks Retry. retry() calls withdrawStaged (4298) -> endStaged marks the record WITHDRAWN and saves the request as resolved 'deny' and resolves its inbox item, but the step stays waiting_for_approval with a pendingRequestId that now points at a closed request. 3a) If the mission has no failed step, retry throws 'No failed step to retry.' (4309) AFTER the staged change was already withdrawn: the refused Retry still destroys the pending change. 3b) If a failed step exists, retry re-arms it and the mission runs, but tick() finds no progressing step and only a waiting one, so it sets waiting_for_user again. 4) respond() rejects any answer with 'This request was already answered.' (3984), so the only remaining exits are Stop or Replan. invalidateDeviceStaging (2582-2593) handles the same state correctly by failing the step; withdrawStaged does not.
verified.evidence: manager.server.ts:2570-2586 (endStaged closes request, no step change); 2597-2600 (withdrawStaged); 4296-4309 (Retry: withdraw at 4298 precedes 'No failed step' throw at 4309); 999-1006 (tick sets waiting_for_user when a step is waiting_for_approval); 3984 (respond refuses closed request); contrast 2582-2593 (invalidateDeviceStaging calls stepFailed on the waiting step).
verified.repair: In withdrawStaged (and endStaged callers that can leave a step waiting), fail the waiting promotion step the same way invalidateDeviceStaging does (setStep running then stepFailed with permission_required), or move the withdrawal after all Retry preconditions pass. Add a test: stage, Retry on a waiting_for_user mission with no failed step (expect refusal and the staged change still STAGED), and stage, Retry with a failed step (expect the promotion step to be failed or re-askable, never waiting on a closed request).

votes.reasoning:
Verified statically against the working tree (no probes run, no repo edits, no npm test).

Confirmed as real:
- endStaged (manager.server.ts:2570-2586) marks the staging record WITHDRAWN and resolves the promotion request with resolution "deny", but never touches the step. It does not move the step out of waiting_for_approval or clear pendingRequestId.
- retry() (4291) calls withdrawStaged at 4298 before the envelope check (4300-4306) and before the "No failed step to retry." throw (4308-4309). When the mission is waiting_for_user with only a waiting promotion step and no failed or blocked step, the staged change is withdrawn and then the Retry is refused. This is the 3a path and it reproduces from the code.
- respond() (3984-3986) refuses any answer to a resolved request ("This request was already answered."), so the waiting step cannot be answered and only Stop or Replan remain. No other code path (reissueStaleAgenticRequests at 2803 skips resolved requests) clears the dead pendingRequestId.
- invalidateDeviceStaging (2582-2593) does fail the waiting step in the equivalent situation, so the contrast with withdrawStaged holds.

Partly inaccurate in the repro:
- 3b says tick finds no progressing step. In fact retry() re-arms failed steps to state "ready" (around 4311-4317), and STEP_LIVE or ready counts as progressing, so evaluate() returns early. The mission then runs the re-armed step. The strand happens only after that step finishes and the dead waiting step is the sole remaining non-done step, at which point tick sets waiting_for_user (999-1006). The end state (stuck with only Stop or Replan) is still reachable, but the mechanism described is not exact.

Severity judgement: this is not an authority issue. The withdrawal is triggered by the workstation operator's own Retry, the staged bytes were never promoted, and no code runs or project write occurs. The harm is a lost pending change on a refused command and a mission stranded until Stop or Replan. That is LOW, not MEDIUM.

The mechanics are real in the working tree, but the finding has no authority impact and its MEDIUM rating is overstated.

Verified by reading src/lib/bunny-missions/manager.server.ts (no probe run):
- retry() at 4291-4309: withdrawStaged runs at 4298, then the envelope check, then the 'No failed step to retry.' throw at 4309. So a refused Retry on a waiting_for_user mission with a pending device promotion still withdraws the staged change. This is a real ordering defect. It is not a bypass: nothing is promoted, and withdrawing on Retry is documented intent (comment at 2597), so only the validate-before-withdraw ordering is wrong.
- endStaged (2570-2586) closes the promotion request as deny but never moves the step, and askPromotion (3873) leaves the step waiting_for_approval with pendingRequestId set. Contrast invalidateDeviceStaging (2589-2591), which fails the step. The stuck-step state is real.
- respond() refuses closed requests (3984), so no answer can be applied to the stale step. Stop and Replan remain available (Replan at 4356 is allowed because STEP_LIVE is only running/verifying, line 55). The stuck step is therefore recoverable and grants no authority.
- Path 3b is described slightly wrongly. After a Retry re-arms a failed step to ready, tick() counts ready as progressing (line 997), so the mission runs. The stall shows up only after the re-armed step finishes: tick then sees only the waiting step and sets waiting_for_user (999-1006).

Net: two real lifecycle/ordering defects (refused Retry destroys a pending unreviewed change; a stale waiting step after Retry). Neither lets the phone gain execution, mutate the project, use revoked authority, or forge identity. The audit record is accurate (request resolved deny with resolvedBy '(withdrawn)'). This is a LOW correctness/availability issue, not a MEDIUM security gap.

verified.title: Full-content staged inspection shows unescaped text, so bidi and invisible characters can reorder what the workstation reviews
verified.boundary: Review integrity between the preview (escaped) and the full inspection (raw). inspectStaged returns bytes.toString('utf8') without escapedText, and the UI renders that string directly in a <pre>.
verified.reproduction: Stage a paired-device change larger than 8192 bytes whose content contains U+202E (RLO), U+2066-U+2069 or U+200B/U+FEFF in the first lines. promotionReason escapes these as ‮ etc. (escapedText, staging.server.ts:180-183), so the request preview is safe. The workstation then clicks 'Inspect all N bytes', which calls mission.staging.inspect; the Host returns the raw string, and the UI renders it in a <pre>. The full view can therefore show text that reads differently from the bytes that will be promoted, and the reviewer's approval is recorded against that view (recordInspection). The sha256 line does not reveal the reordering.

manager.server.ts:2567 (content: bytes.toString('utf8')); src/components/island/mission.tsx:147 (
{shown.content}
); staging.server.ts:180-183 (escapedText used only by promotionReason, manager.server.ts:2541-2552).

verified.title: 8.3 short alias of a dot agent folder is not recognized as an agent-instruction folder

Agent folders such as .opencode, .codebuddy, .grok are not in EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR, so their 8.3 alias (OPENCO~1) escapes AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DIR. Affects the D1 class gate for paired-device writes under a remote envelope, and the promotion-time PHONE_SAFE re-check that relies on the same classifier.

The same write as '.opencode/command/x.md' -> AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS. Under a remote envelope the bus does not refuse the alias write (remoteExecutionRefusal returns null), so the device may answer the ask and the change is staged; promotion re-check (manager.server.ts:2661) also passes because it is PHONE_SAFE. verified.title: Manifest mention check is case-sensitive on a case-insensitive filesystem
verified.boundary: mentionedByManifests (authorization.server.ts:546-552) decides whether a project manifest or workflow names a data path by String.includes on the exact spelling of the write path. NTFS is case-insensitive, so the planner can write the same file under a different spelling and the mention is not found. This defeats the documented invariant that a file a package.json names is EXECUTION_RELEVANT.
verified.reproduction: package.json contains scripts.sync = 'node -e 0 data/config.json'. classifyDeviceWrite('data/config.json', ...) -> EXECUTION_RELEVANT (control). classifyDeviceWrite('DATA/config.json', ...) or 'Data/Config.json' -> PHONE_SAFE_DATA ('JSON or YAML inside a recognized data or document folder'). The write lands on the same file that package.json executes against.
verified.evidence: src/lib/bunny-missions/authorization.server.ts:547-549: needle = rel with '/' separators; variants = [needle, './'+needle, needle with '\\'] and readFileSync(...).includes(variant) with no case folding. Probe output recorded in scratchpad/review-probes/r3 (control EXECUTION_RELEVANT, DATA/config.json PHONE_SAFE_DATA).

Also normalize separators in the manifest text before comparing. Add a test for DATA/config.json against a manifest naming data/config.json.

Scratch project has package.json with scripts.sync = "node scripts/sync.js data/config.json". Results: "data/config.json" -> EXECUTION_RELEVANT (named by package.json); "DATA/config.json" -> PHONE_SAFE_DATA; "Data/Config.json" -> PHONE_SAFE_DATA. The bypass also holds when data/config.json already exists on disk. The cause is that canonical() in paths.server.ts:8-16 uses realpathSync (the JS version, which does not restore on-disk case on Windows) rather than realpathSync.native, so rel keeps the typed spelling. mentionedByManifests (authorization.server.ts:546-553) then does a case-sensitive String.includes against that spelling. The only other case-sensitive step is the same function; the folder regexes use /i, so DATA is still recognized as a data folder. Promotion reclassifies with the same classifier (manager.server.ts:2661-2663), so it inherits the miss and does not independently catch it. The impact is a classification-integrity and invariant gap: a file that package.json names as a tool input is classified as phone-safe data, so it can pass the remote-envelope promotion gate (2663) that EXECUTION_RELEVANT would fail. Real code execution needs the consuming script to read the file as program input, so this stays MEDIUM, not higher.

The phone can write data/cmds.txt, but the sync run needs a workstation-approved command that the device cannot create. The staged bytes are also shown to the workstation for inspection before promotion (manager.server.ts promotion path, REVIEW_BYTES / staging.inspect), so the content is not hidden behind the warning alone. 3. Whether a phone-approved data file could be consumed by an approved workstation run is a property of any data file in any project. export const v = 1
'}) -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'). Control: content beginning 'export const v = 1' -> EXECUTION_RELEVANT ('new content starts like a program or script'). So the heuristic only catches program-first content.

So the defect is demonstrable as a classification bypass, but the harm depends on an unverified project configuration and on the owner missing content they review in full. That fits LOW defense-in-depth, not a phone-code-execution or authority-bypass finding.

export const v = 1
' the classifier reaches the document branch and returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT (line ~615-640). Program-first content ('export const v = 1') is caught as EXECUTION_RELEVANT.
